channel.title: notd: a simple outliner on notd
channel.description: Recent content in notd: a simple outliner on notd

item.title: Quick Start
item.description:
The screen

  • Left sidebar: calendar, search, recent pages, a button to find or create a page, and your extensions.
  • Centre: the current page: its title and its outline of notes.
  • Right sidebar: favorites, backlinks to this page and its child pages.

notd opens on today’s journal page.

Write

Click the text of a note (or the + below the last note) and type. Each bullet is a note, written in Markdown; it is shown formatted as soon as you leave it.

item.title: Kanban Board
item.description:
The kanban board shows every task in your notes as a card, in one column per task state. Dragging a card to another column rewrites the keyword at the start of the note (for example TODO to DOING), exactly as if you had edited the note.

Cards come from notes, so there is nothing to keep in sync: create a task anywhere and it is on the board.

Columns

There is one column per entry in the TASK_STATES setting, in that order (by default TODO, DOING, DONE, SOMEDAY, WAITING, CANCELLED).

item.title: Ping
item.description:
A simple utility endpoint to check if the API is running.

GET /api/v1/ping.php

  • Description: Checks API health.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "pong",
 "timestamp": "2023-10-27T10:30:00+00:00"
}

item.title: Writing Notes
item.description:
Markdown

Notes are Markdown. A note shows the rendered text; click it to edit the source.

  • **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [text](url)
  • #, ##, ### headings
  • lists, quotes, tables and fenced code blocks
  • Shift + Enter for a line break within a note

Brackets and braces are closed automatically as you type; typing the closing one steps over it.

Page links

[[Page Name]]
[[Projects/Alpha]]

Typing [[ suggests existing pages (arrows to choose, Enter or Tab to complete). A link to a page that does not exist yet creates it when clicked. See Backlinks.

item.title: Extensions
item.description:
Retrieves details about currently active extensions.

GET /api/v1/extensions.php

  • Description: Lists active extensions defined in the configuration.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "extensions": [
 {
 "name": "calendar",
 "featherIcon": "calendar"
 },
 {
 "name": "tasks",
 "featherIcon": "check-square"
 }
 ]
 }
}

item.title: Installation
item.description:
Requirements

  • PHP 7.4 or newer with the pdo_sqlite and mbstring extensions (and curl if you use webhooks or the RSS extension).
  • A modern browser.

There is nothing to compile or install.

Run it

Download or clone the repository, then start PHP’s built-in server in that folder:

git clone https://github.com/andjar/notd.git
cd notd
php -S localhost:8000 router.php

Open http://localhost:8000. (router.php keeps the built-in server from handing out the database, the tests and the configuration files.) The database is created on first use and today’s journal page opens with a few welcome notes.

item.title: Journal & Tasks
item.description:
Journal

notd opens on the page for today’s date (for example 2026-11-10). Journal pages are created the first time you open a date, so the journal is simply where you start writing each day.

Move between days with:

  • the calendar in the left sidebar (days with a page are marked; Today jumps back),
  • Ctrl + Alt + Left / Ctrl + Alt + Right for the previous and next day,
  • a link such as [[2026-11-14]].

Tasks

item.title: Attachments
item.description:
Files attached to notes. Files are stored under UPLOADS_DIR in year/month/ folders with a random prefix; the url field of each attachment is where the browser can fetch it.

Uploads are checked against a list of allowed types by extension: jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, pdf, txt, md, csv, json, excalidraw, docx, xlsx, pptx, odt, ods, odp, zip, mp3, m4a, ogg, wav, mp4 and webm. Anything else (HTML, SVG, scripts) is refused, because a browser could run code in it. The limit is 10 MB per file. Several files can be sent in one request (attachmentFile[]); the answer lists the stored ones under attachments and the refused ones under failed.

item.title: Backlinks & Favorites
item.description:
Backlinks

When a note contains [[Page Name]], the page “Page Name” lists that note as a backlink. You never maintain backlinks; they follow from the links you write.

Backlinks appear:

  • in the right sidebar, with the note that contains the link,
  • in the backlinks window (Ctrl + B), which shows each linking note in context.

Pages with many backlinks tend to be the hubs of your notes. A common pattern is to write in the journal and link to the topics you mention; each topic page then collects everything said about it, with dates.

item.title: Core Concepts
item.description:
Pages

A page is a named container of notes. Names are unique and case-insensitive.

  • Journal pages are named after a date (2026-11-10) and are created the first time you open that date.
  • Namespaces. A / in the name creates a hierarchy: Projects/Alpha is a child of Projects, and each page lists its children.
  • A page has its own text and page-level properties, edited through the gear icon next to the title. The same dialog renames the page (links to it are updated, and so are the names of its child pages) and deletes it.

Notes

A note is one bullet in the outline: a piece of Markdown that belongs to a page and optionally to a parent note. Notes have a stable id, which you can use to link to a note (page.php?page=Name#note-<id>) or to embed it elsewhere.

item.title: Operations (write)
item.description:
POST /api/v1/ops.php is the only way to create, change, move or delete notes. The notd frontend uses exactly this endpoint, so anything the UI can do to the outline, a script can do too.

A request carries a list of operations. They are applied in order inside one transaction: either the whole batch is applied or none of it.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/ops.php \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"ops": [
 {"op_id": "demo-1", "type": "create", "id": "0192f6a0-7c3e-7b1a-9f3e-2b1c4d5e6f70",
 "page_id": 87, "parent_id": null, "after": null, "content": "Hello"},
 {"op_id": "demo-2", "type": "edit", "id": "0192f6a0-7c3e-7b1a-9f3e-2b1c4d5e6f70",
 "content": "Hello {status::draft}"}
 ]}'

Operations

Every operation has an op_id (unique string, at most 64 characters), a type and the id of the note it acts on.

item.title: Notes (read)
item.description:
notes.php is read-only. Every change to notes goes through ops.php.

A note looks like this:

{
 "id": "01a1c6b0-ebb1-72da-82de-1d78e583e241",
 "page_id": 87,
 "parent_note_id": null,
 "sort_key": "a0",
 "content": "Project overview {priority::high}",
 "internal": 0,
 "collapsed": 0,
 "active": 1,
 "version": 1,
 "created_at": "2026-11-10 18:20:45",
 "updated_at": "2026-11-10 18:20:45",
 "properties": {
 "priority": [{ "value": "high", "internal": false }]
 },
 "has_attachments": false
}
Field Meaning
id Opaque string, at most 64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -. New notes get a UUIDv7; notes migrated from older databases keep ids such as "123".
parent_note_id Id of the parent note, or null for a top-level note.
sort_key Position among siblings. Siblings are ordered by (sort_key, id) using plain byte comparison. See Ordering.
version Incremented on every change to the note.
properties Index of the properties found in content, grouped by name. internal is true for weight 3 and above.

GET /api/v1/notes.php?page_id={id}

All notes of a page as a flat list, ordered by sort_key, id. Build the tree from parent_note_id.

item.title: Search & Navigation
item.description:
Search

Shortcut What it searches
Ctrl + K Moves to the search field in the left sidebar: full-text search across all notes, with results as you type.
Ctrl + Space Search or create page: find a page by name, or create it if it does not exist.
Shift + Space Note search window (when the cursor is not in a note).

In the result lists, use the arrow keys to move, Enter to open and Escape to close.

item.title: Interface & Shortcuts
item.description:
Layout

Area Contents
Left sidebar Calendar, search, recent pages, Search or Create Page, extensions
Centre Page title, the ☆ favourite star and the gear (page name, text and properties, print, export, lock, delete), then the outline
Right sidebar Favorites, backlinks, child pages
Bottom right Save status

Both sidebars can be collapsed with the arrows at the top. On a phone the sidebars are hidden and a toolbar at the bottom opens them and adds notes.

item.title: Pages
item.description:
A page has a unique name (compared case-insensitively) and its own content, a piece of text whose {key::value} properties become the page’s properties.

Update and delete are sent as POST with _method in the body, so they work on servers that only allow GET and POST.

Read

Request Returns
GET pages.php?name=Name The page with that name. It is created if it does not exist (date names get {type::journal}).
GET pages.php?id=25 One page, or 404.
GET pages.php A list, most recently changed first: ?page, ?per_page (max 100), ?exclude_journal=1. The response has data and pagination.
GET pages.php?names=1 The names of all pages, as an array of strings (&exclude_journal=1 leaves out date pages). Used for link suggestions.
GET pages.php?month=2026-11 The days of that month that have a journal page: [{"date": "2026-11-10", "page_name": "2026-11-10"}]. Used by the calendar.
GET pages.php?date=2026-11-10 Pages with a {date::2026-11-10} property.
GET child_pages.php?namespace=Projects The pages directly below Projects (Projects/Alpha, not Projects/Alpha/Notes).
GET export.php?page=Name The page as Markdown (text/markdown), in Logseq’s layout. &download=1 sends it as a file; ?page_id=25 works too.

A page looks like this:

item.title: Append to Page
item.description:
The simplest way for a script to add notes: no ids, no ordering.

POST /api/v1/append_to_page.php

Appends notes at the end of a page. The page is created if it does not exist (a page named like a date, YYYY-MM-DD, becomes a journal page).

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/append_to_page.php \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{
 "page_name": "My Project",
 "notes": [
 { "content": "Project overview {priority::high}",
 "children": [ { "content": "TODO Research competitors" } ] },
 { "content": "Second note" }
 ]
 }'
Field Meaning
page_name Required. Name of the page.
notes Required. Either a string (one note) or a list of { "content": "...", "children": [...] } objects. children nest to any depth.

Response (200)

item.title: Troubleshooting
item.description:
Problem What to check
A banner says “offline” or the save indicator shows an error The server cannot be reached. Your edits are kept in this browser and are sent when it is reachable again; do not clear the browser’s site data in the meantime.
A change did not appear in another tab or device Reload the page. Tabs in the same browser follow each other; other devices load the current state when the page is opened.
SQL{...} shows an error The query must have one of the three accepted shapes, return note ids and contain no semicolon.
!{{...}} shows nothing The id must be that of an existing note. Use Copy embed code from the note menu instead of typing it. Transclusions deeper than three levels are not expanded.
A property is not found by search Check the syntax: {key::value} with braces and at least two colons. Properties on encrypted pages are not indexed.
A task is missing from the kanban board The keyword must be the first word of the note, in capitals, followed by a space, and be listed in TASK_STATES.
Wrong password on an encrypted page There is no way to recover the content without the password.
An upload is refused Files are limited to 10 MB and to common image, document and text types.
An extension is not in the sidebar Add it to ACTIVE_EXTENSIONS in config.local.php.
The page says the database uses an older schema Run the migration named in the message; see Installation.

For anything else, set NOTD_DEBUG to true in config.local.php, reload, and look at the browser console and the PHP error log.

item.title: Changelog
item.description:
November 2026: version 3.1, schema v4

The database upgrades itself to v4 the first time it is opened.

Writing

  • Enter splits a note at the caret and Backspace at the start of a note joins it with the one above, as in Logseq.
  • Undo and redo for outline changes (Ctrl + Z, Ctrl + Shift + Z), including deleted notes.
  • Zoom into a note (click its bullet) with breadcrumbs back out.
  • [[ page suggestions and / templates share one popup with keyboard navigation; typing a closing bracket steps over the automatic one.
  • Rendered notes support !{{id}} transclusion and SQL{...} queries as read-only embedded outlines.

Pages

item.title: Properties
item.description:
This endpoint is now read-only. It provides a way to query the Properties table index directly, which can be useful for advanced filtering or finding all entities with a specific property value, without needing to perform a full-text search.

GET /api/v1/properties.php

  • Description: Retrieves all indexed properties for a specific entity.
  • Example Call: GET /api/v1/properties.php?entity_type=note&entity_id=42
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "status": [
 { "id": 201, "value": "TODO", "weight": 2, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:30:00" },
 { "id": 205, "value": "DONE", "weight": 4, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:31:00" }
 ],
 "priority": [
 { "id": 202, "value": "High", "weight": 2, "created_at": "2023-10-27 10:30:00" }
 ]
 }
}

item.title: Search
item.description:
Provides powerful search capabilities. It can search by term, find backlinks, list tasks, or list favorited pages.

General Parameters for search types returning notes (e.g., q, backlinks_for_page_name, tasks):

  • include_parent_properties (optional, boolean): Defaults to false. If set to true, each note item in the results array will include a parent_properties field. This field contains an object with aggregated properties from all direct and indirect parent notes. The structure mirrors the main properties field. For search types that do not return notes (e.g., favorites), this parameter has no effect.

GET /api/v1/search.php?q={term}

  • Description: Performs a full-text search across note content. Also supports pagination parameters (page, per_page).
  • Example URL: /api/v1/search.php?q=meeting&include_parent_properties=true
  • Response (200 OK) when include_parent_properties=true: 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "results": [
 {
 "note_id": 42,
 "content": "The full content of the note mentioning the search term.",
 "page_id": 10,
 "page_name": "Project Alpha",
 "content_snippet": "... with the search <mark>term</mark> highlighted ...",
 "properties": { "status": [{"value": "TODO"}] },
 "parent_properties": { "project_code": [{"value": "Alpha"}] }
 }
 ],
 "pagination": { "total_items": 1, "current_page": 1, "per_page": 20, "total_pages": 1 }
 }
}
  • If include_parent_properties is false (default), the parent_properties field will be an empty object ({}) or null.

The Search endpoint also supports other modes:

item.title: Query Notes
item.description:
Runs a SQL query that selects note ids and returns the matching notes. This is what SQL{...} blocks in notes use.

The query runs on a read-only connection. Unless ADVANCED_QUERY_MODE is enabled in the configuration, it must also:

  • start with one of these forms:
    • SELECT id FROM Notes WHERE ...
    • SELECT [DISTINCT] N.id FROM Notes N JOIN Properties P ON N.id = P.note_id WHERE ...
    • SELECT id FROM Notes WHERE id IN (SELECT note_id FROM Properties WHERE ...
  • contain no semicolon and none of the words INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, TRUNCATE, ALTER, EXEC, CREATE, ATTACH, DETACH;
  • only refer to these columns when using a table prefix: id, content, page_id, parent_note_id, created_at, updated_at, sort_key, version, collapsed, active (Notes) and note_id, name, value, weight (Properties).

The first selected column must be the note id. Do not add LIMIT; use page and per_page.

item.title: Templates
item.description:
Templates are plain Markdown files in assets/template/note/ and assets/template/page/. They are text only: nothing in them is executed.

List

GET templates.php?type=note&tz=Europe/Oslo

{"status": "success", "data": [{"name": "meeting", "content": "## Meeting 2026-11-11\n- Attendees: "}]}

Placeholders are filled in when listed, in the time zone given by tz (the server’s otherwise): {{date}}, {{time}}, {{datetime}}, {{year}}, {{month}}, {{day}}, {{weekday}}, {{timestamp}}, {{random}}, {{uuid}}. Date placeholders take a PHP date format: {{date:d.m.Y}}.

Create, update, delete

POST templates.php {"type": "note", "name": "daily-review", "content": "## Review\n- "}
POST templates.php {"_method": "PUT", "type": "note", "current_name": "daily-review", "new_name": "review", "content": "..."}
POST templates.php {"_method": "DELETE", "type": "note", "name": "review"}

Names may contain letters, digits, - and _. Creating a name that exists answers 409.

item.title: Webhooks
item.description:
Manages webhook subscriptions. A webhook is an HTTP POST that notd sends to a URL of your choice when a property changes.

  • Deliveries are sent after the change has been saved, never while the database is locked, and not at all if the change was rolled back.
  • Only verified and active webhooks receive events: call the verify action once after creating a webhook.
  • Each delivery carries the headers X-Notd-Event and X-Notd-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 of the body with the webhook’s secret).
  • PUT and DELETE can also be sent as POST with "_method": "PUT" or "_method": "DELETE" in the JSON body.
  • Set WEBHOOKS_ENABLED to false in the configuration to stop all deliveries.

POST /api/v1/webhooks.php (Create)

  • Description: Registers a new webhook.
  • Request: application/json 
    {
 "url": "https://example.com/webhook-receiver",
 "entity_type": "note",
 "property_names": ["status", "priority"],
 "event_types": ["property_change", "entity_created"]
}
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "id": 1,
 "url": "https://example.com/webhook-receiver",
 "entity_type": "note",
 "property_names": ["status", "priority"],
 "event_types": ["property_change", "entity_created"],
 "secret": "whsec_... (only shown on creation)",
 "...": "..."
 }
}

POST /api/v1/webhooks.php?action=test&id=1

  • Description: Sends a test event to the specified webhook.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "message": "Test event sent. Check history for result."
 }
}

GET /api/v1/webhooks.php?action=history&id=1

  • Description: Retrieves the delivery history for a webhook.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": {
 "pagination": { "total": 1, "page": 1, "limit": 20 },
 "history": [
 {
 "id": 1,
 "webhook_id": 1,
 "event_type": "test",
 "payload": "{\"event\":\"test\",...}",
 "response_code": 200,
 "response_body": "{\"status\":\"ok\"}",
 "success": 1,
 "created_at": "2023-10-27 11:00:00"
 }
 ]
 }
}

GET /api/v1/webhooks.php (List)

  • Description: Lists all configured webhooks.
  • Response (200 OK): 
    {
 "status": "success",
 "data": [
 {
 "id": 1,
 "url": "https://example.com/webhook-receiver",
 "entity_type": "note",
 "property_names": ["status", "priority"],
 "event_types": ["property_change", "entity_created"],
 "active": 1,
 "verified": 1,
 "last_triggered": "2023-10-27 11:00:00"
 }
 ]
}
